parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the cooling of water in different sized beakers. Refer to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Pour an estimated 75 cm 3 of hot water into beaker A. Use the markings on the beaker as a guide. Place the thermometer in the water in beaker A. Record, in the first row of Table 1.1, the temperature θ of the water at time t = 0 and immediately start the stop-watch. Record the temperature θ of the water at times t = 30 s, t = 60 s, t = 90 s, t = 120 s, t = 150 s and t = 180 s. Remove the thermometer from the beaker. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text: θ for beaker A decreasing and recorded to at least 1 °C

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Repeat the procedure in (a)(i) for beaker B. [2]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the average cooling rate x for beaker B. Use your readings for beaker B in Table 1.1 and the equation x = θ 0 – θ 180 T where T = 180 s and θ 0 and θ 180 are the temperatures of the water in beaker B at t = 0 and t = 180 s. Include the unit for the cooling rate. x = ......................................................... [1]

with unit °C / s
